name: 32-card Poker
description: 32-card Poker (French Poker) is draw poker using a 32-card stripped deck (7-A). 2-5 players. 5 cards each. Blinds, betting, draw up to 4, final betting, showdown. Key difference: Flush BEATS Full House (flushes are rarer). A can be low (A-7-8-9-10 straight valid). Suit ranking may break ties: ♥>♦>♣>♠.

history.origins: 32-card Poker is a draw poker variant that uses the traditional 32-card deck (seven through ace in each suit), the same pack used for Piquet and other European games. It is popular in Southern Europe and is sometimes called Stripped Deck Poker. The game adapts standard five-card draw to the shortened deck and alters hand rankings so that flushes rank above full houses, since flushes are rarer with fewer cards. The variant reflects regional preference for the piquet-style deck.
timeline: 20th century: documented as a French poker variant played with the 32-card piquet deck.

rules.objective: Form the best five-card poker hand; the highest-ranked hand at showdown wins the pot. Hand order differs from standard poker: flush ranks above full house in the 32-card deck.
rules.gameplay: Blinds. Deal 5. Betting round. Draw up to 4 cards. Final betting. Showdown. Altered rankings: Flush > Full House (flushes rarer in 32-card deck). A can be low: A-7-8-9-10 = valid straight. Suit ranking may tiebreak.

strategy.basic: Flush pursuit is more valuable than in standard 52-card poker because flushes are rarer in the 32-card deck.
strategy.intermediate: Understand stripped-deck probabilities: straights and flushes are more common, while full houses are slightly less frequent than in a full deck.
strategy.advanced: Track suit distribution to leverage the suit ranking tiebreaker; avoid drawing into easily dominated flushes when opponents likely hold higher suits.
tips: Hands that would be marginal in a 52-card game, such as medium flushes, gain value because flushes are rarer in the 32-card deck.
Because players may draw up to four cards, be cautious about slow-playing strong but fragile hands before the draw.
When using suit order as a tiebreaker, prefer building flushes in higher-ranking suits and avoid committing heavily with weak-suit flushes.
